### J-1 Drill-down writes no file, but NFR-2 allows caches
- quote: "writing no file; the pane draws its drill-down from that output only."
- quote: "other than the caches the CLI already keeps under `.nio/cache/`"
- situation (consistency): the cost-so-far path writes a cache under `.nio/cache/` in the way NFR-2 permits. FR-21 says the `show --json` command writes no file at all. A tester reading FR-21 alone would fail a run that writes a cache, and a reader of NFR-2 cannot tell which rule wins for `show --json`.
- fix: say in FR-21 "writing no file except the caches of NFR-2", or drop the cache exception from NFR-2 if `show --json` must not touch `.nio/cache/`.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: FR-21 now writes no file except the NFR-2 caches; AC-23 says .nio/cache/ is ignored

### J-2 Empty-section wording differs between FR-12 and the ACs
- quote: "a "none yet" line for the section"
- quote: "the section holds a "no jury yet" line"
- quote: ""no tasks yet" line"
- situation (consistency): FR-12 gives one required line, `"none yet"`. AC-9 requires `"no jury yet"` and AC-11 requires `"no tasks yet"`. A pane that prints `none yet` in the juries section passes FR-12 and fails AC-9 as written.
- fix: pick one wording and use it in FR-12 and both ACs, or say that the line names the section, for example "no jury yet" and "no tasks yet".
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: FR-12 line names the section; AC-9 says no juries yet

### J-6 Context use cannot come from the only source the pane may use
- quote: "the pane draws its drill-down from that output only"
- quote: "on Claude Code it is the context window's fill in percent"
- situation (logic): the host exposes context use (AC-16). The pane must show it. FR-21 limits the pane to the `nio flow show --json` output. AC-23 fixes that output to five keys: timeline, juries, tasks, cost and memory. None of them can hold the session's context fill, which belongs to the host session and not to the effort. The pane either breaks FR-21 or cannot satisfy FR-11 and AC-16.
- fix: say where the context figure comes from, or add a sixth key to the JSON and its source.
- validation: confirmed: FR-21 says the pane draws from `flow show --json` only, AC-23 fixes five keys with no context key, yet FR-11 and AC-16 need the host's context fill; no other text names a source.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: delegated grill Q11: context from host; old nio shows update line (FR-28, AC-30); failed review defined by evidence.passed (FR-3, AC-2); error JSON + exit 1 (FR-27, AC-29)

### J-7 "Writes no file" contradicts the allowed caches
- quote: "writing no file"
- quote: "other than the caches the CLI already keeps under `.nio/cache/`"
- situation (logic): `nio flow show <slug> --json` runs and the CLI refreshes a cache under `.nio/cache/`. FR-21 says no file is written. NFR-2 allows it. AC-23 checks `git status --porcelain`, which passes only if the cache is ignored. A strict reading of FR-21 fails on the cache write.
- fix: give FR-21 the same cache exception as NFR-2, or say the cache is untracked.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: FR-21 now writes no file except the NFR-2 caches; AC-23 says .nio/cache/ is ignored

### J-8 Cost per stage and per jury is undefined for repeated stages and overlap
- quote: "a stage's share being the events between its entry and exit in `history.jsonl`, and a jury's the juror and refuter agents whose run belongs to that gate"
- situation (logic): an effort goes back from review to implementing, so a stage is entered twice. Or the effort is still in its current stage, which has an entry and no exit. Or a jury runs inside the spec stage. The spec does not say whether the two entries are summed, whether the open stage counts to now, or whether the jury's tokens are counted again in the stage. AC-12 can then give two different correct totals for the same events.
- situation (testability): the effort is unfinished, so its current stage has an entry and no exit, and AC-12 only has finished stages. A test cannot say whether the open stage is counted up to now, left out or shown as `-`. Events outside any entry/exit pair, or a juror whose run belongs to no gate, also have no stated outcome.
- fix: define the rule for a re-entered stage, the open stage, and whether jury cost is included in or separate from the stage.
- validation: confirmed: FR-7 defines a stage's share as entry-to-exit events only. Nothing says how a re-entered stage, the open stage or jury cost inside a stage is counted, and AC-12 does not fix it.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: delegated grill Q9: FR-7, AC-12, AC-28 define visits, open stage, unattributed, jury breakdown

### J-9 Skipping the mods reports "skipped" even when they are already installed
- quote: "| claude | skip | - | - | → skipped | [human] |"
- quote: "IF the human chose to skip the mods THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL install neither."
- situation (logic): the mods are already installed and the human picks skip. The table row says the closing message reads "skipped". The mods are in fact installed. The message gives a false state. FR-18 and the table row `claude | install | yes` treat the installed state, but the skip row ignores it. The state is also undefined when a mod is installed at user scope and not local (FR-25).
- fix: either make the skip row depend on "already installed", or say the message means "not touched".
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: delegated grill Q10: nio mods install CLI step (FR-29), install ACs on its output and skill text; skip row split by already installed

### J-11 Two features in one spec should be an epic with slices
- quote: "This spec adds a drill-down to the"
- quote: "It also makes `@nio:install` on Claude Code install the NIO Claude Code mods"
- situation (scope): one gate jury covers 26 FRs and 27 ACs. If the drill-down's cost figure (FR-7, FR-8, FR-21) fails review, the mod install (FR-15 to FR-26) is blocked with it, although the install needs none of the drill-down code. The reverse also holds: the install can be right and the drill-down still held back.
- fix: split into an epic with two slices, one for `@nio:install` and the mods (FR-15 to FR-20, FR-22 to FR-26, AC-18 to AC-22, AC-25 to AC-27), one for the drill-down (FR-1 to FR-14, FR-21, AC-1 to AC-17, AC-23, AC-24), with the slice order stated.
- validation: refuted: The Summary ties both parts together as one [human] scope from issue #142, and `epic` is empty by choice. The two parts share no requirement, but the spec as written is a deliberate single spec, not a defect of the text.

### J-12 Local scope install conflicts with the maintainer's "set up once for the team"
- quote: "install them for this clone only (Claude Code's `local` scope), changing no file to commit"
- quote: "NIO set up once for the whole team, with hosts, models, budgets and permission prompts chosen for everyone."
- situation (scope): the maintainer runs `@nio:install` once in the repo. A teammate (P-2) clones it and gets no mods, so the pane and the drill-down are missing for them until they run install on their own clone. The persona's "set up once for the whole team" is not met, and the spec does not say so. The intake's goal "nobody has to run ... by hand" is only met per clone.
- fix: state the trade-off in UJ-2 and in the Decisions entry: each clone runs install once, and say which of the two wins. If the team should get the mods once, a committed (project-scope) install is needed, which FR-25 rules out, so the human must choose.
- validation: confirmed: FR-25 gives local scope per clone, tagged [agent]. A-3 and the persona's "set up once for the team" are not reconciled, and UJ-2 and Decisions state no trade-off.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: delegated grill Q7: local scope kept, trade-off stated in UJ-2 and Decisions

### J-13 Memory filter in FR-10 is not the one the human asked for, and may not match `nio pack` / `nio query`
- quote: "those whose `paths` name a file under the effort's spec folder or whose `against` names the effort"
- quote: "Observable: the listed IDs equal those `nio pack` / `nio query` return for the effort."
- situation (scope): a decision record about `src/nio/pack.py`, with no `paths` entry under the spec folder and no `against` naming the effort, is returned by `nio pack` for this effort but is not listed in the drill-down. AC-15 then fails although FR-10 was built as written. The reverse can also happen. FR-10 is tagged [human], but the human's words only name `nio pack` / `nio query` as the source.
- situation (testability): `nio pack` and `nio query` rank by relevance and use the embedding model, while FR-10 selects by `paths` and `against` from the front matter. A record that matches by `paths` but is not returned by `nio query` makes the AC-15 test fail although FR-10 holds. A query hit that has neither `paths` nor `against` makes AC-15 pass although FR-10 is broken. The AC doesn't test the FR.
- fix: either make FR-10 say "the records `nio pack` returns for the effort" (and read them without the embedding model if that is possible), or retag FR-10 as [default] and state the filter rule as a decision the grill must confirm.
- validation: confirmed: FR-10 filters on `paths` and `against` front matter, while AC-15's observable is equality with `nio pack` / `nio query`, which rank by relevance. The two sets can differ, so the AC does not test the FR.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: delegated grill Q8: front-matter filter kept, FR-10 retagged agent, AC-15 checks the filter

### J-14 `nio flow show --json` covers four sections the issue did not ask to change
- quote: "WHEN asked with `nio flow show <slug> --json` THE SYSTEM SHALL print, as one JSON object, the effort's timeline, juries, tasks, cost so far and memory, writing no file; the pane draws its drill-down from that output only."

A project whose `nio` on PATH is an older version has no `flow show --json`, and FR-23 covers only a missing `nio`, not an old one, so the pane shows nothing useful there.

### J-15 Numeric speed target nobody asked for

### J-17 "Failed review" is never defined
- quote: "WHEN the effort's history holds a failed review THE SYSTEM SHALL show it in the timeline with its reason."
- quote: "Given a history with a failed review"
- situation (testability): the spec doesn't say which `history.jsonl` entry is a failed review: a field value, an event kind, or a stage change back. A test author must guess the fixture, and one reading shows a review that another reading treats as an ordinary stage change. A failed review with no recorded reason is also uncovered.
- fix: name the history field and value that mark a failed review, and give the output when the reason is missing.
- validation: confirmed: FR-3 and AC-2 never name the `history.jsonl` field or value that marks a failed review, and the output when the reason is missing is not given.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: delegated grill Q11: context from host; old nio shows update line (FR-28, AC-30); failed review defined by evidence.passed (FR-3, AC-2); error JSON + exit 1 (FR-27, AC-29)

### J-18 Install ACs observe an agent transcript, not a deterministic output
- quote: "no mod question in the transcript"
- quote: "the skill asks exactly one question about the mods"
- situation (testability): `@nio:install` is a markdown skill that a model follows, and these ACs are marked `integration`. "Exactly one question" and "no question" depend on model behaviour, so a run can pass once and fail the next with no code change. No harness or fixture is named that makes it repeatable. The same applies to "the closing message holds the mod's name and error" in AC-21.
- fix: say how each is checked, either as a fixed script or CLI step that is unit-tested, or as an e2e with a recorded tolerance. Or move the question count out of the AC.
- validation: confirmed: AC-22 and AC-26 observe "the transcript" and the number of questions the markdown skill asks, with level integration and no harness named. This depends on model behaviour and is not repeatable.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: delegated grill Q10: nio mods install CLI step (FR-29), install ACs on its output and skill text; skip row split by already installed
